settings.title: Settings
approvals.select: Select an approval to see it.
approvals.why_unknown: No rule or reasoning recorded for this one.
approvals.reject_reason: Why? (the agent records it on the order)
approvals.email.subject: Subject
approvals.changes.review: Needs a person's review; not applied automatically.
approvals.plan.review: Review the plan line by line
cases.no_runs: No agent runs recorded on this case.
exceptions.acted: Follow-up started; watch the case timeline.
planning.empty: No planning runs yet. The daily plan runs every morning.
planning.approved: {n} line(s) approved; the planner is writing them.
planning.ranking_better: {name} scores higher than the reference supplier.
settings.models_hint: Changes apply to the next run, without a restart. Greyed models lack an API key on this host.
settings.h.rfq_no_reply_days: Comma-separated: one follow-up per value, then a person takes over.
settings.f.po_eta_request_before_days: Ask to confirm the delivery date this many days before
settings.f.po_late_days: Late order: request an ETA after, escalate after (days)
settings.h.po_late_days: Two values: days past the planned date.
settings.f.max_actions_per_run: Max emails + escalations per follow-up run
settings.f.auto_send_partner_ids: Odoo partner ids whose emails go out without approval
settings.h.auto_send_partner_ids: Comma-separated partner ids. Empty means every email is approved by a person.
settings.planning_hint: Empty keeps the ABC class defaults. A value replaces them for products a planner has not tuned.
settings.no_history: No versions saved yet; the environment's values apply.
task.resolve_unlinked: Match an email to an order
settings.auto_kinds: Email kinds sent without approval, for every supplier
settings.auto_kinds_hint: Ticked kinds go out as soon as the agent drafts them; the rest wait for an approver. RFQs and purchase orders are best left ticked off until you trust the wording.
chat.title: Talk to your AI
chat.empty: Ask what is going on, or tell your AI what to do. It answers from the case, the order and the policy; instructions are shown for confirmation before anything happens.
chat.placeholder: Why is this late? · Ask them for a firm date · Wait until the 20th · Close this, I cancelled the order
chat.thinking: The Director agent is looking at the case…
chat.action.request_eta: Ask the supplier for a delivery date
chat.action.hold_until: Hold the case until a date
chat.action.link_email: Link the email to an order
settings.h.ignored_senders: Addresses or domains, comma-separated (for example accountprotection.microsoft.com, member_services@outlook.com). Their emails never become cases.
board.title: Orders board
board.col.hint.proposed: Draft requests for quotation, from the planner or made in Odoo. Drag one to “Quotation requested” to send it.
board.col.hint.rfq_sent: The request went to the supplier; the agent reminds them on the policy's days.
board.col.hint.quote_received: The supplier answered with prices or dates; someone must accept the change.
board.col.hint.confirmed: Confirmed orders whose delivery is still far away.
board.col.hint.incoming: Delivery due in the next few days, or late. Receipts are recorded in Odoo.
board.col.hint.received: Received in the warehouse, waiting for the supplier's invoice.
board.col.hint.closed: Done or cancelled in the last 30 days.
board.move.not_allowed: That column follows Odoo and the supplier's answers; it cannot be set by hand.
board.move.receive_in_odoo: Receipts are recorded in the warehouse, in Odoo; the card moves by itself.
board.mark_confirmed: Mark as confirmed by the supplier
board.role_hint: Approvers can move cards and act on them.
board.drawer.no_case: The agents have not worked on this order yet. Emails and reminders will show here.
board.act.late_po: Ask the supplier for a delivery date now, instead of waiting for the policy's day.
board.act.rfq_no_reply: Send the reminder now, instead of waiting for the policy's day.
board.acted: Started; the outcome lands in the history below in a moment.
notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.empty: Nothing new since you opened the app.
board.col.hint.invoicing: Received orders whose invoice is being checked or already drafted as a bill; drag to “Closed” to lock the order.
approvals.bill.all_ok: Every line matches the order and what was received.
approvals.bill.never_posted: Approving records a draft bill in Odoo. Nothing is posted: accounting posts it.
approvals.scores.writes: Approving writes the scores on each supplier, the observed lead times on the price list and the planner's parameters.
suppliers.title: Suppliers
suppliers.intro: Scores from the weekly run: on-time in-full, observed lead time, reply time and receipt problems over the last twelve months. Click a supplier for the scorecard.
suppliers.empty: No scorecards yet. The performance agent runs every Monday at 07:00; the run waits for approval in the inbox.
suppliers.no_scorecard: No scorecard text for this run.
approvals.autonomy.intro: {by} wants to widen what the agents do without asking. A second person confirms it; approving saves the policy below as a new version.
approvals.autonomy.rule: Rules are read top to bottom; the first that matches decides. Nothing matched means a person decides.
settings.auto_send_moved: Which emails, changes and bills run without approval is decided by the autonomy policy.
autonomy.title: Autonomy
autonomy.intro: Rules decide which proposed actions run alone. Everything else waits for a person. Raising autonomy needs a second person; lowering it applies at once. What ran alone shows below and can be reverted while its window is open.
autonomy.pending: Change #{id} by {by} is waiting for a second person ({rules}).
autonomy.rules_hint: Top to bottom, first match wins. A condition the agent cannot prove never matches: an unknown amount or score keeps the action with a person.
autonomy.no_rules: No rules: every action is approved by a person.
autonomy.preview_summary: With these rules, {alone} of the {total} approvals of the last {days} days would have run alone.
autonomy.needs_second: Approval #{id} created: another person must confirm the wider rules ({rules}).
autonomy.feed.title: Done automatically
autonomy.feed.hint: What the agents did by rule, without asking. Revert what should not have happened while its window is open.
autonomy.feed.empty: Nothing ran alone in the last {days} day(s).
board.drawer.origin_planning: Proposed by the daily plan of {date}
board.drawer.lines_unavailable: The order lines could not be read right now.
learning.suggestions_hint: Every Monday the system reads the last 90 days of approvals: what you always approve unchanged, what you always reject, what tolerance would have matched. Accepting a rule still goes through a second person.
learning.no_suggestions: No suggestions yet. They appear after enough decisions of the same kind.
learning.accepted_approval: Approval #{id} created: a second person confirms the new rule.
learning.stats_summary: {total} decisions in the last {days} days: {unchanged} approved unchanged, {edited} edited, {rejected} rejected.
suppliers.profile.title: How we write to this supplier
suppliers.profile.saved: Profile saved; the next email follows it.
planning.held_hint: The planner rejected this rule change twice; it is not proposed again until then.
planning.keep_params: Keep these parameters for this product when approving
playbooks.title: Playbooks
playbooks.intro: A playbook is the sequence the Director agent follows on an order: ask, wait, chase, then hand over. Steps are fixed in code; the agents write the emails and a person approves what the autonomy rules do not cover. Each card shows how many orders sit on each step.
playbooks.trigger.po_late: when a confirmed order is late
playbooks.trigger.rfq_silent: when a quotation request gets no answer
playbooks.trigger.discrepancy: when a receipt does not match the order
playbooks.start.title: Start a playbook
playbooks.start.hint: The daily follow-up job starts late-order and silent-RFQ playbooks by itself; start one by hand to act today.
playbooks.cancelled: Playbook on {po} cancelled; the order stays with a person.
playbooks.runs.empty: No playbook is running. The follow-up job starts them when an order is late or a quotation request goes unanswered.
approvals.playbook_intro: This approval is step {n} of {total} in the playbook "{title}". Approving lets the plan go on:
approvals.award.direct: Direct order to an alternative supplier
approvals.award.freight: freight estimate {pct}% added to quoted prices
approvals.award.writes: Approving confirms the chosen supplier's RFQ as an order; the other suppliers get a courteous decline and their RFQs are cancelled.
approvals.award.writes_direct: Approving creates and confirms an order to the chosen supplier at the list price.
approvals.offer.bounds: Between {floor} and {current}; the cap keeps it there.
approvals.offer.writes: Approving sends the counter-offer email through the supplier agent; nothing changes on the order until the supplier answers.
approvals.partner.name: Company name
approvals.partner.name_hint: Suggested from the sender's domain; change it before approving.
approvals.partner.writes: Approving creates the vendor in Odoo and an RFQ with the quoted lines whose reference matches a product; the email is linked to it.
sourcing.title: Quote rounds
sourcing.intro: A round invites the best-ranked suppliers through the supplier agent, collects their quotes and asks a person to award. Start one on an order to requote its lines.
sourcing.empty: No quote round yet. Start one on an RFQ from its drawer or here.
sourcing.start.title: Start a quote round
sourcing.start.hint: The order's lines are quoted by the top suppliers of the ranking; its own supplier keeps the original RFQ.
sourcing.drawer.round_hint: Invite the best-ranked suppliers to quote these lines
sourcing.drawer.offer_hint: Ask the supplier for a better price on the quoted line, within the cap
settings.sourcing_hint: How many suppliers a round invites and how long it waits; the freight estimate on quoted prices; the limits a counter-offer never leaves.
settings.f.negotiation_cap_pct: Counter-offer cap (% below the quoted price)
settings.h.negotiation_cap_pct: A person never sees an offer further below the quote than this.
risk.title: Risk radar
risk.intro: Where stock may run out in the next 30 or 60 days and which suppliers may deliver late. The odds come from the forecast and the open orders. One click starts the right sourcing move; a person approves the result.
risk.act_alternate_hint: Asks other suppliers for the line behind {po}; you approve the award.
risk.act_round_hint: Starts a quote round for {qty} units; you approve the award.
calendar.title: Demand calendar
calendar.intro: Promotions, holidays and projects the planner cannot see in the history. Past events are taken out of the history; events ahead raise the forecast.
calendar.added: {name} added; the next plan uses it.
calendar.f.name: Name
whatif.title: Portfolio what-if
whatif.intro: Change the service level or the review period of a whole class and see the totals before approving. Nothing is written.
planning.consolidation: Consolidation: ordering {days} days early saves {freight} of freight and costs {stock} in stock.
settings.f.holding_cost_pct_year: Holding cost (% of value per year)
settings.h.holding_cost_pct_year: Used to decide whether pulling an order forward is cheaper than paying freight twice.
suppliers.profile.freight_hint: Order value from which this supplier ships free, and what freight costs below it. The planner pulls orders forward when that beats holding the stock.
approvals.request.writes: Approving creates one request for quotation per supplier with the ticked items and answers the requester in the same email thread. Unticked and unmatched items are left for a buyer.
approvals.pricelist.intro: {partner} sent {source}: {changed} price(s) change, {unmatched} row(s) match no product we buy.
approvals.pricelist.writes: Approving records the ticked rows on the supplier's price list in Odoo. Orders already confirmed keep their prices.
settings.h.internal_senders: Addresses or domains, comma-separated. Their emails to the mailbox are read as internal purchase requests, matched to the catalogue and proposed as RFQs.
briefing.title: Morning briefing
briefing.none_yet: No briefing yet. The Director agent writes one every weekday at 07:30.
briefing.none_yet_build: No briefing yet. The Director agent writes one every weekday at 07:30; build today's now if you want it earlier.
briefing.no_paragraph: The sections below stand on their own today; the Director agent's paragraph could not be written.
briefing.email_hint: Addresses, comma-separated; empty sends to the recipients in Settings
assistant.title: Ask your AI
assistant.empty: Ask about the whole department: which orders are at risk, how a supplier is doing, what a product's forecast says, what ran alone. Or give an instruction: it becomes a plan you confirm once, and every step then goes through the usual agents and approvals.
assistant.placeholder: Which orders are at risk this week? · How is Proveedor Hidraulica doing? · Start a quote round for CBEA-LHN, 40 units
assistant.thinking: The Director agent is reading the desk…
settings.h.briefing_recipients: Addresses, comma-separated. Every weekday at 07:30 the briefing is emailed to them from the bot mailbox; empty means nobody, the page still shows it.
home.title: Home
supplier.no_scorecard: No scorecard yet: the performance agent scores suppliers every Monday.
supplier.no_prices: No prices on record for this supplier.
supplier.emails_hint: Dates and links only; the text stays in Outlook.
supplier.no_emails: No emails linked to this supplier's orders.
ai.title: AI performance
ai.intro: How much the department runs alone, how fast people decide, how good the predictions are and what the agents cost. Every number comes from records; a dash means the period holds no data.
ai.edit_hint: share of approvals a person changed first
ai.rejection_hint: share of decisions that said no
ai.eta_hint: mean drift between promise and delivery
palette.title: Command palette
palette.placeholder: Order, supplier, page… or a question for your AI
push.enabled: You will be notified of new approvals on this device.
push.denied: The browser did not allow notifications.
approvals.bulk.title: Bulk decisions
approvals.shortcuts: j/k move · a approve · r reject · e edit
approvals.diff.title: Your changes
board.age_hint: Days since the order was created
board.predicted_hint: Predicted delay from this supplier's usual drift; confidence from its OTIF
demo.title: Demo mode
demo.reset_done: The demo is back at the start.
demo.not_ready: Some steps cannot run on this machine
playbook.internal_request.description: The requester was acknowledged when the request was approved. Send the quotation request to the supplier, tell the requester when the order is confirmed and when the goods are received; stop quietly when neither happens within the waits.
playbook.internal_request.step.send_rfq: Send the request for quotation to the supplier
playbook.internal_request.step.wait_conf: Wait for the order to be confirmed
playbook.internal_request.step.tell_conf: Tell the requester the order is confirmed
playbook.internal_request.step.tell_rece: Tell the requester the goods arrived
playbook.late_order.description: Ask the supplier for a new delivery date, wait two days, chase once more, wait again, and when nothing comes propose an alternative source. Closes itself when the goods arrive.
playbook.late_order.step.ask_eta: Ask the supplier for a new delivery date
playbook.late_order.step.wait_reply: Wait two days for a reply
playbook.new_supplier_onboarding.descrip: A buyer confirms the partner, the sourcing agent brings the quote into the round, and the first order is watched more closely. Until the sourcing agent is deployed (phase 11 S4) the steps escalate to a buyer.
playbook.new_supplier_onboarding.step.co: A buyer confirms the new supplier
playbook.quote_round.description: The sourcing agent sends the same request to the best-ranked suppliers, collects the quotes and proposes an award. Until the sourcing agent is deployed (phase 11 S4) the step escalates so a buyer runs the round.
playbook.quote_round.step.run_round: Send the request to the best-ranked suppliers
playbook.quote_round.step.wait_quotes: Wait five days for the quotes
playbook.quote_round.step.compare: Compare the quotes and propose an award
playbook.receipt_variance.description: The logistics agent reported the difference. Wait three days for the supplier's answer, chase once, then escalate so a buyer settles it (credit note, replacement or acceptance).
playbook.receipt_variance.step.wait_answ: Wait three days for the supplier's answer
playbook.silent_rfq.description: Remind the supplier, wait three days, remind once more, wait four days, then escalate so a buyer decides whether to call or to quote elsewhere.
playbook.silent_rfq.step.remind: Remind the supplier about the quotation
playbook.silent_rfq.step.wait_reply: Wait three days for the quote
playbooks.cond.unsent_rfq: the request was not sent yet
